proved_step: LEMMA (rank-r DP, subclass lane D). Let U in Z^{m x r}, A in Z^{r x n} with all |A_ik| <= a, t in Z^m, v in Z^m, T in Z, and f(x) = [sum_j v_j [U_j . (A x) >= t_j] >= T] for x in {0,1}^n. Then #{x : f(x)=1} is computed EXACTLY by the DP C_0 = {0 -> 1}, C_i(y) = C_{i-1}(y) + C_{i-1}(y - A_i) (A_i = i-th column of A), followed by the sum over y of C_n(y) [top(y) >= T], where top(y) = sum_j v_j [U_j . y >= t_j]. Correctness: f depends on x only through y = Ax, so the count equals sum_y N(y) g(y) with N(y) = #{x: Ax = y} = C_n(y) by the recurrence. Cost: each support set has entries in [-i a, i a]^r, so |supp C_i| <= (2 i a + 1)^r and the total time is O(n m r (2na+1)^r) arithmetic operations on integers of O(log(n a m)) bits. Consequence: for r <= (1-eps) n / log2(2na+1) and a <= poly(n) the time is 2^{(1-eps) n} poly(n, m), a saving of 2^{eps n} = n^{omega(1)} over brute force on the subclass of THR o THR circuits whose bottom weight matrix has rank at most r. Verified only on the tested cases (405 exact checks, n <= 12, r in {1,2,3}; cm-2cd5c456ea174b3b). Scope: this is the rank class only; it does not transfer to general THR o THR of size n^alpha, so it does not by itself meet the Chen-Tal-Wang threshold.

proved_step: S0002 LEMMA (column-sparse correction of the rank-r DP; closes sub-item (i) of G0001). Let W in Z^{m x n}, |W_ji| <= a, v,t in Z^m, T in Z, f(x) = [sum_j v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T]. Let S subset [n], |S| = s, B = [n]\S, q = n-s, and let r = rank of W restricted to columns B (r may be 0). Let A in Z^{r x q} be r linearly independent rows of W_B (so |A_ik| <= a), and U in Q^{m x r} with W_B = U A (exists because the rows of A span the row space of W_B). Let C_0 = {0:1}, C_i(y) = C_{i-1}(y) + C_{i-1}(y - A_i), where A_i is the i-th column of A. Then #{x in {0,1}^n : f(x)=1} = sum over xi in {0,1}^S and y in Z^r of C_q(y) * [sum_j v_j [U_j.y >= t_j - W_{jS}.xi] >= T]. PROOF: write x = (x_B, xi). Then W_j.x = U_j.(A x_B) + W_{jS}.xi, so the indicator depends on x_B only through y = A x_B. By induction on i (split on the last bit), C_i(y) = #{x' in {0,1}^i : A_{<=i} x' = y}, so summing over xi and y gives the count. COST: |y_k| <= q a, so supp C_i lies in [-ia, ia]^r, size <= (2qa+1)^r; total 2^s (2qa+1)^r * O(q m r) operations on numbers of poly(n, log a) bits (U rational, thresholds compared exactly). CONSEQUENCE: if s + r log2(2qa+1) <= (1-eps) n - O(log n), then time 2^{(1-eps) n} poly(n,m), a saving of n^{omega(1)} for constant eps. Special cases: s = 0 gives S0001; r = 0 gives 2^s. SCOPE LIMIT: for generic full-rank W (r = q, a >= 1) the condition fails, since s + q log2(2qa+1) > n; so no saving on generic instances, and this does NOT meet the Chen-Tal-Wang threshold by itself. Corrects the turn-5 wording: the 2^s factor enumerates xi in {0,1}^S, not 'distinct y-values'. lemma: RESIDUAL-DP PROCEDURE (lane D, THR o THR bottom-layer counting). Setting: n variables split into prefix S (|S| = s) and bottom block B (|B| = q = n - s). Bottom gates j = 1..m have integer weights W_j in [-a,a]^n, thresholds t_j, output weights v_j, target T. For a prefix x_S put r_j = t_j - W_{j,S}.x_S, lo_j = sum_{i in B} min(0, W_{ji}), hi_j = sum_{i in B} max(0, W_{ji}), c = sum of v_j over {j : r_j <= lo_j}, N = {j : lo_j < r_j <= hi_j}. Then #SAT(prefix) = #{x_B in {0,1}^q : c + sum_{j in N} v_j [W_{j,B}.x_B >= r_j] >= T}. Procedure: DP over the bottom variables with state z in Z^N, z_j = partial sum of W_{j,B}.x_B; the state box has size prod_{j in N} (hi_j - lo_j + 1) <= (2aq+1)^{|N|}. Time O(q |N| (2aq+1)^{|N|}) per prefix, times 2^s prefixes.

lemma: NECESSARY CONDITION FOR THE RESIDUAL-DP SAVING (lane D). Setting as in S0007: prefix S (|S| = s), bottom block B (|B| = q), gate j with W_j = (W_jS, W_jB), t_j, lo_j = sum_{i in B} min(0, W_ji), hi_j = sum_{i in B} max(0, W_ji), L_j = sum_{i in S} min(0, W_ji), U_j = sum_{i in S} max(0, W_ji). Define the always-live set C = {j : lo_j < t_j - W_jS.x_S <= hi_j for every x_S in {0,1}^s}. Then (a) j in C iff t_j - U_j > lo_j and t_j - L_j <= hi_j; (b) C is contained in N(x_S) for every prefix x_S, so |N(x_S)| >= |C|. Consequently the residual-DP corollary (|N(x_S)| <= kappa q / log2(2aq+1) for all prefixes) forces |C| <= kappa q / log2(2aq+1). PROOF: (a) W_jS.x_S ranges over [L_j, U_j] and both endpoints are attained (x_S = indicator of the negative, resp. positive, weights), so the residual t_j - W_jS.x_S ranges exactly over [t_j - U_j, t_j - L_j]; it lies in (lo_j, hi_j] for all x_S iff t_j - U_j > lo_j and t_j - L_j <= hi_j. (b) If j in C, every residual lies in (lo_j, hi_j], so gate j is not clipped for any prefix and belongs to N(x_S) by definition. The consequence is immediate from (b). So the residual-DP procedure can save only on families where almost all gates are clipped for most prefixes; a family where a constant fraction of gates is in C is outside its saving regime, whatever the prefix split.
gap: G0001(iii) is now sharpened: the open question is whether hard instances of the m = n^alpha family can have |C| = O(q / log(2aq+1)) for most prefix splits, i.e. thresholds far enough outside the weight range that most gates are clipped. Random instances with thresholds in the middle range violate it (see evidence). Open: a family-level bound on |C| that the adversary cannot avoid.

Let lo_j = sum_{i in B} min(0, W_ji), hi_j = sum_{i in B} max(0, W_ji), L_j = sum_{i in S} min(0, W_ji), U_j = sum_{i in S} max(0, W_ji). Let C = {j : lo_j < t_j - W_jS.x_S <= hi_j for every x_S in {0,1}^s}. Then j in C iff (t_j - U_j > lo_j and t_j - L_j <= hi_j).

proved_step: CLAIMED. Proof: the values W_jS.x_S over x_S in {0,1}^s form a subset of [L_j, U_j] whose minimum and maximum are attained (at x_S = indicator of the negative, resp. positive, weights). The condition 'for all x_S, lo_j < t_j - W_jS.x_S <= hi_j' says that the set of attained residuals lies in the interval (lo_j, hi_j]. A set lies in an interval iff its minimum and maximum lie in it. The residual minimum is t_j - U_j and its maximum is t_j - L_j, so the condition is t_j - U_j > lo_j and t_j - L_j <= hi_j. Consequence: every j in C is not clipped for any prefix, so C is contained in N(x_S) for every x_S, and |N(x_S)| >= |C|. Hence the residual-DP corollary |N(x_S)| <= kappa q / log2(2aq+1) forces |C| <= kappa q / log2(2aq+1).

lemma: Bookkeeping identity for the clipping route (not progress by itself). For a THR o THR gate j with prefix S (size s) and bottom block B (size q), let N_j(x_S) be the event that the gate is unclipped, i.e. lo_j less than t_j minus W_jS.x_S at most hi_j. Then the expected number of unclipped gates over uniform x_S equals the sum over gates j of the mass of the window {v : t_j minus hi_j at most v less than t_j minus lo_j} under the distribution of W_jS.x_S. Hence E|N(x_S)| is at least the sum over gates of the minimum window mass over integer thresholds t_j.

Such tail placements make the bottom layer nearly constant and are the easy case. The open point (G0009 case ii, G0001 iii, G0006) is therefore whether every hard instance family must place many gates with windows covering a constant fraction of prefixes. proved_step: LEMMA (rank-after-deletion DP; repairs the open generalisation G0001(i)). Let f(x) = [sum_j v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T] with W an m x n integer matrix, all |entries| <= a, and let C be any column set with |C| = c. Put W' = W restricted to the columns outside C, n' = n - c, and k = rank_Q(W'). Then #f can be computed exactly in time 2^c * poly(m, n) * (2 a n' + 1)^k. PROOF: (1) For each of the 2^c assignments x_C, the bottom thresholds become integers t'_j = t_j - W_j|C . x_C. (2) Pick k linearly independent rows B_1..B_k of W' (integer). Each row W'_j = sum_l c_jl B_l with rational c_jl, computed exactly once. (3) Process the n' free variables in a fixed order. The state after a prefix is y = (B_l . x_prefix)_l. Its coordinates satisfy |y_l| <= a * (prefix length), so at most (2 a n' + 1)^k states occur per prefix; each step adds B_l[i] * bit to y. (4) At the end, W'_j . x = sum_l c_jl y_l, so f(x) = [sum_j v_j [c_j . y >= t'_j] >= T] depends on x only through y. A DP with multiplicities summed over states gives the exact count. (5) Summing over the 2^c branches gives the count. CONSEQUENCES: (a) If W = P + E with rank_Q(P) <= r and E supported on a set of columns C, then k <= r, giving the S0002 column-sparse bound. (b) If E is supported on rows R x columns C of a bipartite vertex cover, then for j not in R the rows of W' agree with P' (rank <= r), so k <= r + |R| and the time is 2^c (2 a n' + 1)^(r + |R|). (c) Choosing C adaptively to minimise c + k log2(2 a n' + 1) gives exponent min_C [ c + k(C) log2(2a(n-c)+1) ]. LIMITS: for generic full-rank W, k = n', and the bound is 2^c (2an'+1)^(n'), which is worse than brute force when a >= 1. The lemma closes only the bounded-vertex-cover case of G0001(i). Entrywise-small (norm-sparse) E and the full-rank case G0001(iii) remain open.

Let 1 <= c <= n and r = rank of the m x c prefix block W[:, 1..c]. Then #F = sum_x F(x) is computed exactly in time O(2^(n-c) (2ac+1)^r m (n+r)) plus poly(m,n) preprocessing. Proof: choose rows J_1..J_r of W[:,1..c] forming a basis of its row space (greedy elimination over Q). For every row j there is a unique lambda_j in Q^r with W_j,[1..c] = sum_i lambda_ji W_J_i,[1..c]; compute it by exact elimination and clear denominators (integer vector lamInt_j and denominator d_j). Write x = (y, z), y in {0,1}^c, z in {0,1}^(n-c). Put sigma(y)_i = sum_k W_J_i,k y_k. Then W_j.x = lambda_j.sigma(y) + tail_j(z), tail_j(z) = sum_k W_j,c+k z_k, so F(x) depends on y only through sigma(y). Let N(s) = #{y : sigma(y) = s}; by |sigma_i| <= ac the support of N has at most (2ac+1)^r points and is computed by a DP over the c columns. Cost matches the bound. Remark: the earlier rho-sparse-row extension is a special case, because exceptional rows raise the rank of the prefix block and are absorbed into r. Saving over 2^n requires r log2(2ac+1) <= (1-eps) c, i.e. prefix-block rank o(c / log c) with c = omega(log n). Generic instances have rank min(c, m), so this gives no saving for them. Let W = BC + E in Z^{m x n} with B in Z^{m x r}, C in Z^{r x n}, all entries of B, C, W bounded in absolute value by M, and E nonzero only on rows R (|R| = k) and column c0. (3) Each coordinate of Cx and W_R x lies in [-Mn, Mn], so the number of states S satisfies S <= 2 (2Mn+1)^{r+k}. Time O(n * S * m * (r+k)). Consequence: #SAT in time 2^n / n^{omega(1)} whenever (r+k) log2(2Mn+1) <= n - omega(log n). proved_step: RANK-r DP THEOREM (ALGORITHM). Setting: W in Z^{m x n}, |W_ji| <= B, rank(W) = r; integers t_j, v_j, T; f(x) = [sum_j v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T] on {0,1}^n; #SAT = #f^{-1}(1). ALGORITHM: (1) choose r rows C_1..C_r of W forming a basis of the row space (exact Gaussian elimination over Q); choose pivot columns P with C[:,P] invertible. (2) For each j put lambda_j^T = W_j[P] (C[:,P])^{-1}; then W_j = lambda_j^T C exactly (verified). Clear denominators: A_j = D*lambda_j in Z^r, TH_j = D*t_j, D a positive integer. (3) DP: table of pairs (y, cnt), start {(0,1)}; for i = 1..n replace the table by {(y,c) and (y + C[:,i], c)} with equal y merged by summing counts. (4) Output sum of cnt over table entries y with [sum_j v_j [A_j.y >= TH_j] >= T]. CORRECTNESS: y(x) = Cx, so W_j.x = lambda_j.y(x), and A_j.y >= TH_j iff W_j.x >= t_j (D > 0). By induction the table after variables 1..l holds the fibre counts of y_l = sum_{i<=l} C[:,i] x_i, so step (4) equals sum_x f(x). COMPLEXITY: |table_l| <= min(2^l, (2Bl+1)^r) since |y_{l,k}| <= B l. Time = poly(n, m, r, log B, bitsize(t,v)) * min(2^n, (2Bn+1)^r), where the bit sizes of A_j, TH_j are poly(r, log B) by Cramer's rule. COROLLARY 1: if B <= n^{O(1)} and r <= (1-eps) n / log2(2Bn+1), the time is 2^n * 2^{-eps n} * poly(n,m) = 2^n / n^{omega(1)}. COROLLARY 2: if r = o(n / log n) and B = poly(n), the time is 2^{o(n)} poly(m). m = n^alpha is arbitrary. SCOPE: exact for every W; for full-rank W the state bound is 2^n, so there is no saving. This is a counting algorithm on a restricted class, not a circuit lower bound and not a P vs NP statement. Barrier label: no barrier is relevant to a counting algorithm on a restricted class. lemma: Lemma Z (zonotope bound on distinct Cx). Let C in Z^{r×n} with |C_{k i}| <= M and V = {C x : x in {0,1}^n}. Then |V| <= sum_{j=0}^{r} binom(n, r-j) binom(r, j) (M sqrt{r})^{r-j}. In particular |V| <= 2^{r+1} (n M sqrt{r})^{r}.
evidence: Brute force check on 144 random instances confirms the inequality (cm-07093975a4a34380, violations 0). The zonotope volume derivation is standard and reproduced above.
proved_step:
statement: Let c_i in Z^r be columns of C. Put Z = sum_{i=1}^n [0,c_i] subset R^r. Then V subset Z cap Z^r. Let W = Z + sum_{k=1}^r [0,e_k]. If p != q in V then the unit cubes p+[0,1]^r and q+[0,1]^r have disjoint interiors and are contained in W. Hence |V| <= vol(W). W is the zonotope generated by generators c_1..c_n, e_1..e_r. For any r-subset S of generators, |det S| = 0 if S is linearly dependent, otherwise by Hadamard |det S| <= prod_{v in S} ||v||_2. Hence vol(W) = sum_{S, |S|=r} |det S|. Count subsets with j unit vectors and r-j columns: binom(r,j) binom(n,r-j). For such S, prod ||v|| <= (M sqrt{r})^{r-j} *1^j. Summation gives the stated bound. Using binom(n,k) <= n^k and binom(r,j)<=2^r and sum_{i=0}^r a^i <=2 a^r for a=n M sqrt{r} >=2, we obtain |V| <= 2^{r+1} (n M sqrt{r})^r, so log2 |V| <= r (log2(n M)+1/2 log2 r+1)+1. Thus |V| <= 2^{(1-epsilon)n} whenever r (log2(n M)+O(log r)) <= (1-epsilon)n. This is the same regime as the box bound (2 M n+1)^r up to constant factors.
proof: Induction on i for the partial DP is immediate: after processing i columns the set of possible partial sums lies in the box [-M i, M i]^r, size at most (2 M i+1)^r. Volume argument above gives the zonotope refinement. The Hadamard bound and counting of generator subsets give the stated inequality. Checking on 144 random instances with n in {6,8,10,12}, r in {1,2,3}, M in {1,2,5} gives 0 violations of the inequality (cm-07093975a4a34380).

lemma: CLIPPING LEMMA (residual DP). Let W in Z^{m x n}, t, v in Z^m, T in Z, n = l + k, 0 <= l < n. For x = (y,z) with y in {0,1}^l, z in {0,1}^k, write P = W[:,:l], R = W[:,l:], and f(y,z) = [sum_j v_j [W_j.(y,z) >= t_j] >= T]. Put c_j(y) = P_j.y, lo_j = sum_i min(R_ji,0), hi_j = sum_i max(R_ji,0), theta_j(y) = clip(t_j - c_j(y), lo_j, hi_j+1). Then (a) f(y,z) = g_{theta(y)}(z) with g_th(z) = [sum_j v_j [R_j.z >= th_j] >= T]; (b) #f^{-1}(1) = sum over th in U of cnt(th) * #{z : g_th(z) = 1}, where U = {theta(y)} and cnt(th) = #{y : theta(y) = th}; (c) |U| <= min(2^l, prod_j (||R_j||_1 + 2)).
evidence: cm-987e810552b34cda: 36 exploratory instances (n in {10,12,14,16}, seeds 1-3, random B, m, t, v, T). lemma_residual_mismatch = 0, clipped_vs_unclipped_mismatch = 0, alg_vs_brute_mismatch = 0, key_bound_violations = 0 (|U| <= 2^l and |U| <= prod(||R_j||_1+2) held in every instance). proved_step: PROOF. (a) For every z, R_j.z lies in [lo_j, hi_j]. If t_j - c_j(y) <= lo_j then theta_j = lo_j and both [R_j.z >= t_j - c_j] and [R_j.z >= lo_j] equal 1. If t_j - c_j(y) >= hi_j + 1 then theta_j = hi_j + 1 and both equal 0. Otherwise theta_j = t_j - c_j(y) and the two conditions coincide. Since W_j.(y,z) = c_j(y) + R_j.z, every gate indicator agrees with the clipped one, so f agrees. (b) Group the prefixes y by theta(y) and apply (a). (c) theta_j takes at most hi_j - lo_j + 2 = ||R_j||_1 + 2 values, so U lies in a product set of that size; trivially |U| <= 2^l. COROLLARY: #f^{-1}(1) is computable in time poly(n,m) * (2^l + 2^k * |U|). SCOPE: a saving below 2^n needs |U| <= 2^{l - delta}. The product bound gives this only if m * log2(a+2) <= (1 - delta') l, where a bounds ||R_j||_1. For m = n^{1.5} with weights in [-B,B] (||R_j||_1 of order kB), the product bound exceeds 2^l, so the lemma gives no saving in the target regime. It does NOT close G0001(iii) or G0006, the open family-level bound on live gates.

lemma: RANK-r COUNTING PROCEDURE. Let W in Z^{m x n} with |W_ji| <= M, rank_Q(W) = r >= 1, t, v in Z^m, T in Z, and f(x) = [sum_j v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T] for x in {0,1}^n. Let N = #f^{-1}(1). Then N can be computed exactly in time poly(n, m, log M) * min(2^n, (2Mn+1)^r) arithmetic operations on integers of bit length poly(n, m, log M). COROLLARY: for r = o(n / log n) and M = O(1), N is computed in time 2^n / n^{omega(1)} when r = omega(1); for r <= (1-delta) n / log2(2Mn+1), time <= 2^{(1-delta) n} poly(n,m).

proved_step: PROOF. (1) Choose r linearly independent rows of W; call them C (r x n, integer, |C| <= M). Every row W_j lies in rowspace(C), so W_j = B_j C for a unique B_j in Q^r; compute B (Gaussian elimination over Q; poly bit size) and a common denominator D, so DB_j is integral. statement: PREFIX-RANK STATE BOUND. Let W in Z^{m x n} with |W_ji| <= M, t in Z^m, v in Z^m, T in Z. For x in {0,1}^n define the threshold circuit f(x) = [sum_j v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T]. For each prefix length k = 0..n, let S_k = {W_{1..k} . a : a in {0,1}^k} be the set of distinct partial sums of the first k columns. Let r_k = rank_Q(W_{1..k}) be the rational rank of the first k columns. Then |S_k| <= min(2^k, (2Mk+1)^{r_k}). Moreover, #SAT(f) can be computed by a dynamic program that maintains the exact counts for each element of S_k, and the total number of DP states over all k is sum_k |S_k| <= sum_k min(2^k, (2Mk+1)^{r_k}).
proof: For any a in {0,1}^k, W_{1..k}.a is an integer vector in Z^m with each coordinate bounded by Mk in absolute value (since |W_ji| <= M and a_j in {0,1}). Hence W_{1..k}.a lies in the box [-Mk, Mk]^m, which contains (2Mk+1)^m points. However, the image of {0,1}^k under the linear map W_{1..k} is contained in the Q-linear span of the columns of W_{1..k}, which has dimension r_k. The intersection of a box of side 2Mk+1 with an r_k-dimensional linear subspace over Q has at most (2Mk+1)^{r_k} integer points (a basis of the subspace gives an injective linear map to Q^{r_k}, and integer points map to integer points whose coordinates are bounded by the same box after a change of basis with determinant 1). Therefore |S_k| <= min(2^k, (2Mk+1)^{r_k}). The DP processes columns 1..n sequentially; at step k it stores the exact count of assignments a in {0,1}^k for each s in S_k. The transition from k to k+1 is s' = s + b * W_{*,k+1} for b in {0,1}. The final count for f(x)=1 is obtained by evaluating the threshold conditions on the full sum s in S_n and summing the corresponding counts. Correctness follows by induction on k.

proved_step: LEMMA (M-free rank bound on bottom patterns). Let W in Q^{m x n} have rank r, t in Q^m, and P(W,t) = {(1[W_j.x >= t_j])_{j<=m} : x in {0,1}^n}. Then |P(W,t)| <= min(2^n, sum_{i=0}^{r} C(m,i)). PROOF. Factor W = U V with U in Q^{m x r}, V in Q^{r x n} (rank r). Put z = Vx. Then W_j.x = U_j.z, so the pattern is a function of z in the finite set Z = {Vx : x in {0,1}^n} subset of Q^r. Let D = {U_j.z - t_j : j, z in Z} and delta = min{|d| : d in D, d != 0} > 0 (finite set of rationals; if D = {0} there is no sign change to track). Choose eps in Q with 0 < eps < delta and t_j - eps not equal to U_j.z for all j and z in Z (finitely many exclusions). For z in Z: 1[U_j.z >= t_j] = 1[U_j.z > t_j - eps], because U_j.z >= t_j implies U_j.z > t_j - eps, and U_j.z < t_j implies U_j.z <= t_j - delta < t_j - eps. The hyperplanes H_j = {z : U_j.z = t_j - eps} avoid Z, so each z in Z lies in an open cell of the arrangement {H_j} in R^r, and the pattern is determined by that cell. Distinct patterns come from distinct cells. Rows U_j = 0 give constant sign and define no hyperplane; dropping them leaves m' <= m hyperplanes. A central fact (Buck 1943; Zaslavsky 1975): an arrangement of m' affine hyperplanes in R^r has at most sum_{i<=r} C(m',i) <= sum_{i<=r} C(m,i) cells. Hence |P| <= sum_{i<=r} C(m,i). Also |P| <= 2^n trivially. QED. COROLLARY: sum_{i<=r} C(m,i) <= (m+1)^r = 2^{r log2(m+1)}, so for m = n^alpha and r(alpha log2 n + 1) <= (1-eps) n the number of bottom patterns is at most 2^{(1-eps)n}, for every weight size M.

Output = sum over x_rest and s of count(s) * [sum_i u_i [(W_rest x_rest)_i + a_i s >= t_i] >= T]. Correctness: the summand depends on x only through (x_rest, z). Time 2^{n-k} * poly(n, m, k, M'). This is 2^{n-k} poly, strictly better than the spec's 2^{n-k/2} meet-in-the-middle bound when the weights are polynomially bounded. Correction of my earlier S0055: that block-DP restates the rank-r DP of R0805 / S0002 (branch on the complement, DP on the rank block) and is not new. Only this rank-one improvement is new content.

Hence #distinct residuals F|rho <= min(2^p, prod_j (hi_j - lo_j + 2)).

ALGORITHM (rank-one block DP, CLAIMED, pending review). Let W be an integer m x n matrix with entries bounded by M, and let J be a set of k columns with W_ij = a_i v_j for all i and j in J. For x = (x_J, x_R) we have (Wx)_i = (W_R x_R)_i + a_i z, where z = sum over j in J of v_j x_j. Procedure: compute count_J(s) = #{x_J : z = s} once by a DP over J with states in [-kM', kM'] (M' = max |v_j|). Then enumerate x_R in {0,1}^(n-k) and output the sum over integers s of count_J(s) times [sum_i u_i [(W_R x_R)_i + a_i s >= t_i] >= T]. Correctness: the summand depends on x only through (x_R, z). Time: 2^(n-k) times O(m k^2 M') arithmetic operations. This saves a factor 2^k over brute force, which is better than the spec's 2^(n-k/2) meet-in-the-middle bound. Scope: it helps only when a constant fraction of the columns is proportional, and it does not apply to full-rank families (k = 0). Classification correction: this is the block-DP of S0055 specialised to a rank-one block (branch on the complement, DP on the block). It is NOT a special case of S0002, which branches on the touched columns and runs the rank-r DP on the rest. lemma: RANK-r BOX-BOUND DP. Let W in Z^{m x n} have rank r and all |W_ji| <= B. Choose a row index set R with |R| = r whose rows form a basis of the row space, and let A = W_R (integer, |A_ki| <= B). For each j there is C_j in Q^r with W_j = C_j^T A (exact, since W_j lies in the row space). Then for all x in {0,1}^n: W_j . x = C_j . (A x). Hence #SAT f = sum_y c(y) g(y), where y = A x, c(y) = #{x : Ax = y}, g(y) = [sum_j v_j [C_j . y >= t_j] >= T]. The DP over columns i = 1..n keeps a dictionary {y: c(y)} and adds column A_i (for x_i = 0 and 1). The number of keys after step i is at most prod_k (sum_{i' <= i} |A_{k i'}| + 1) <= prod_k (||A_k||_1 + 1) <= (nB + 1)^r, because coordinate k of every partial sum lies in the integer interval [sum_i min(0, A_ki), sum_i max(0, A_ki)] of length ||A_k||_1. Also keys <= 2^n. So the total running time is poly(n, m) * min{2^n, (nB+1)^r} with exact rational arithmetic. Consequence: for r <= (1 - delta) n / log2(nB + 1), the time is 2^{(1-delta) n} * poly(n, m), i.e. a saving of 2^{delta n} / poly over brute force. This refines the earlier (2na+1)^r bound, since ||A_k||_1 <= n a.
gap: Scope limits: (a) the saving needs r log2(nB+1) <= (1-delta) n, so it does not reach full-rank W (r = n gives 2^n, G0001(iii) and G0003 stay open); (b) it needs bounded integer weights B; for unbounded weights the box bound is not poly; (c) the rank-r window only lies inside the 2^{(1-delta) n} regime for r = O(n / log(nB)); near-low-rank W (G0001(i), G0013) remains open. Obligation G0002 is closed only for this bounded-weight rank-r family; the open question is whether a general rank-r bound on the number of distinct A x values exists without bounded weights.

proved_step: COLUMN-DELETION RANK LEMMA. Let W in Z^{m x n} with |W_ji| <= B. Let S subset [n], |S| = s, R = [n] minus S, and suppose rank(W_R) <= r, where W_R is W with the columns in S deleted. Let A be a set of rank(W_R) rows of W_R forming a basis of its row space. Entries of A are rows of W, so |A_ki| <= B. For each row j there is C_j in Q^r with W_jR = C_j^T A (exact, since W_jR lies in the row space). For x in {0,1}^n write x = (x_R, x_S). Then W_j . x = C_j . (A x_R) + W_jS . x_S. Let c(y) = #{x_R : A x_R = y} and g(z) = [sum_j v_j [z_j >= t_j] >= T], with z_j = C_j . y + W_jS . x_S compared exactly over Q. Then #{x : g(Wx)} = sum over x_S in {0,1}^s of sum over y of c(y) g(C y + W_S x_S). The DP over the columns of R keeps the dictionary {y: c(y)} and adds column A_i for x_i in {0,1}. Coordinate k of every partial sum lies in an integer interval of length ||A_k||_1 <= |R| B, so the number of keys is at most prod_k (||A_k||_1 + 1) <= (|R| B + 1)^r, and also at most 2^{|R|}. Hence the total time is O(2^s (|R| B + 1)^r poly(m, n)) with exact rational arithmetic. Special cases: s = 0 is the rank-r DP lemma (Q-9d5ab93ad8 lemma). If W = C A + E with E having k nonzero entries in total, then deleting the at most k columns touched by E leaves a matrix of rank <= r, so s <= k and the time is 2^k (nB+1)^r poly. This beats 2^n when k + r log2(nB+1) <= (1 - delta) n.

lemma: EXCEPTIONAL-ROW DP (exact). Let W in Z^{m x n} with all |W_ji| <= B. Partition the rows into a normal set N (|N| = m-k) whose submatrix W_N has rank r with a row basis R (|R| = r, A = W_R), and k exceptional rows X with block E = W_X (arbitrary, |E_qi| <= B). For each j in N there is C_j in Q^r with W_j = C_j^T A (exact). For x in {0,1}^n let s(x) = (A x, E x) in Z^r x Z^k. Then W_j . x = C_j . (A x) for j in N, and W_X x = E x, so f(x) = [sum_{j in N} v_j [C_j.(Ax) >= t_j] + sum_q v_{X,q} [(Ex)_q >= t_{X,q}] >= T] is a function of s(x) alone. Let c(y,z) = #{x in {0,1}^n : s(x) = (y,z)}. Then #SAT f = sum_{(y,z)} c(y,z) g(y,z) with g the indicator above. The column DP that adds (A_i, E_i) for x_i in {0,1} computes c exactly (induction on the prefix length). Each coordinate of y lies in an integer interval of length ||A_k||_1 and each coordinate of z in an interval of length ||E_q||_1, so the number of keys is at most prod_k(||A_k||_1+1) prod_q(||E_q||_1+1) <= (nB+1)^{r+k}, and also <= 2^n. Hence #SAT f is computed exactly in time poly(n,m) * min{2^n, (nB+1)^{r+k}} with rational arithmetic for C_j. COROLLARY: this is the rank-rho bound with rho = r+k, applied to a basis that includes the exceptional rows; it adds no saving beyond rank(W) <= r+k.
gap: G0001(iii) stays open: this procedure gives a saving only when rank(W) = r+k < n/log2(nB+1). The frontier families (sharp_sat, uniform / 0/1 / sparse 0/1 weights) have full rank n at n = 12..18 (cm-f4b3650aebec4998), so no saving. G0001(i) (approximate low-rank part with bounded error) is NOT closed: exact handling of k exceptional rows costs (nB+1)^k in the z-part, so a saving needs k small or clipping of z (only [z_q >= t_q] matters), which is unproved. Repair idea (not yet proved): clip each z_q to the interval where [z_q >= t_{X,q}] is undecided over the remaining columns; the state count then drops to a function of the remaining-column weights. Open.

proved_step: LEMMA (column-deletion rank-r reduction). For W in Z^{m x n} with |W_ji| <= B and r >= 0, define rho_r(W) = min{|S| : rank(W restricted to columns [n] minus S) <= r}. Then for any thresholds t, weights v >= 0 and T, the count #SAT = #{x in {0,1}^n : sum_j v_j [W_j . x >= t_j] >= T} equals sum over x_S in {0,1}^S of #{x' in {0,1}^{[n]\S} : sum_j v_j [W'_j . x' >= t_j - W_{j,S} . x_S] >= T}, where W' = W restricted to [n]\S. Each inner count is a count for the rank-<=r matrix W' with integer thresholds, so the rank-r box-bound DP applies to it, giving total time 2^{rho} * poly(n,m) * (nB+1)^r for a set S attaining rho. PROOF: partition x = (x_S, x'); the gate condition W_j . x >= t_j is equivalent to W'_j . x' >= t_j - W_{j,S} . x_S, and the outer sum over x_S is exhaustive. The identity holds for every S, not only the minimal one; minimality only minimises the 2^{|S|} factor. Corollary (E = W - W0 with rank(W0) <= r and at most e nonzero entries): S = columns touched by E gives rho_r(W) <= e, so the cost is 2^e * poly * (nB+1)^r, and S can be found by enumerating column sets of size <= e (n^e choices), giving a promise-free algorithm of time n^{O(e)} * 2^e * poly * (nB+1)^r. This subsumes S0002 (column-supported E) and covers entrywise-sparse E.

lemma: CLIPPED EXCEPTIONAL-ROW DP. W in Z^{m x n}, |W_ji| <= B; normal rows N with rank r and row basis R, A = W_R; k exceptional rows X with block E = W_X. For a prefix length p let L+_q(p) = sum_{i>p} max(0,E_qi), L-_q(p) = sum_{i>p} min(0,E_qi), and clip z_q to c_q(z,p) = clamp(z_q, t_q - L+_q(p) - 1, t_q - L-_q(p)). Then (a) #SAT f is computed exactly by the DP over keys (y_p, c(z_p,p)), where y_p = A x_{<=p} and z_p = E x_{<=p}; (b) the number of keys at step p is at most min{ 2^p, prod_k(||A_k^{<=p}||_1+1) * prod_q(L+_q(p)-L-_q(p)+2) }. Proof of (a): for any future suffix delta in [L-,L+] the indicator [z_q+delta_q >= t_q] is unchanged by clamping z_q, so keys with equal (y, clipped z) have identical future weights; the transition commutes with clipping by the same argument at p+1. Proof of (b): y-coordinates lie in integer intervals of length ||A_k^{<=p}||_1; clipped z-coordinates lie in an integer interval of length L+-L-+1. Scope: exact for any integer W; the bound improves the constant over (nB+1)^{r+k} but gives no exponent saving for fixed k, and nothing for full-rank W (G0001(iii) stays open).

lemma:
SETTING. W in Z^{m x n}, |W_ji| <= B. Thresholds t_j in Z. Let K be a set of k rows and N its complement, with rank_Q(W_N) = r. The DP is the clipped-state DP of the record: after reading x_1..x_p its key is (cnt, tuple of (j, clipped s_j) over undecided gates), where s_j = W_j^{<=p} . x_{<=p}, cnt = number of decided-true gates, and the clip is clamp(s_j, t_j - L+_j(p) - 1, t_j - L-_j(p)). The DP is exact (record lemma (a); its proof is that the clipping preserves the decision for every suffix in [L-, L+]; I re-checked this step by hand and it holds).

CLAIM 1 (state bound). Choose r independent rows of W_N as A in Z^{r x n}; every row of W_N is U_j A with U_j in Q^r. For every p, the number of keys at step p is at most (m+1) (2pB+1)^r prod_{q in K} ((n-p)B+3).
Proof. (i) For normal j, s_j = U_j . y with y = A x_{<=p} in Z^r and |y_i| <= pB. So the set of undecided normal gates and their clipped values are functions of y, and y has at most (2pB+1)^r values. (ii) For q in K, the key either omits q, or holds a clipped value in an integer interval of length L+_q(p) - L-_q(p) + 2 <= (n-p)B + 2, since the suffix l1 mass is at most (n-p)B. That gives at most (n-p)B+3 options. (iii) cnt takes at most m+1 values. The key is a function of (cnt, y, the k clipped values), so the bound follows.

CLAIM 2 (algorithm). Run the DP forward for p = 1..n. The answer is the total weight of keys with cnt >= T, where T = ceil(m/2) (or any fixed threshold). Each step loops over at most S_p keys, 2 choices of x_p, and m gates. By CLAIM 1, S_p <= (m+1)(2nB+1)^r (nB+3)^k <= (m+1)(2nB+3)^{r+k}. lemma: Structured-support state lemma. Let n, m, r >= 1, B >= 0 be integers. Let A be an r x n integer matrix with entries in [-B, B], U an arbitrary m x r integer matrix, and E an m x n integer matrix whose nonzero columns all lie in a fixed set T of size s. Put W = UA + E. For a prefix length p <= n, the prefix state of x in {0,1}^p is the vector (W_{j,<=p} . x_{<=p}) over j in [m]. Claim: the number of distinct prefix states over x in {0,1}^p is at most min(2^p, (2Bp+1)^r * 2^{|T cap [p]|}). Consequently, if s + r*log2(2Bn+1) <= (1-eps) n, every prefix state count is at most 2^{(1-eps) n}.

proved_step: Proof. For j in [m] and x in {0,1}^p: W_{j,<=p} . x = sum_{i<=p} (sum_k U_{jk} A_{ki}) x_i + sum_{i<=p} E_{ji} x_i = sum_k U_{jk} y_k + sum_{i in T cap [p]} E_{ji} x_i, where y = A_{<=p} x_{<=p} in Z^r. So the whole state vector is a function of the pair (y, x restricted to T cap [p]). Since |y_k| <= B p, y takes at most (2Bp+1)^r values; the restriction takes at most 2^{|T cap [p]|} values. Counting pairs gives the bound; the bound 2^p is trivial. Since p <= n, (2Bp+1)^r <= (2Bn+1)^r, and 2^s (2Bn+1)^r = 2^{s + r log2(2Bn+1)} <= 2^{(1-eps) n} under the stated condition. Sanity check: with s = 0 (pure rank r) it recovers the rank-r state bound. Scope: exact, for any m; T is one fixed set for the whole matrix, not per row. Not covered: per-row k-sparse E whose supports together cover all columns (the union support is then all n columns, so s = n).

proved_step: CLAIMED (R0953). ROW-OUTLIER RANK LEMMA (row-sparse case of G0001(i)). Setting: W in Z^{m x n}, |W_ji| <= B_W; t in Z^m; T in Z; a set K of exceptional rows with |K| = k; every j outside K has W_j = U_j A with U_j in Z^r and A in Z^{r x n}, |A_ic| <= B_A (rows of A fixed, the same for all normal rows). Statement: N = #{x in {0,1}^n : sum_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T} can be computed exactly by a DP whose number of states after reading x_1..x_p is at most (k+1)(2pB_A+1)^r ((n-p)B_W+1)^k. Hence N is computed in time poly(n,m) (k+1) (2nB_A+1)^r (nB_W+1)^k. In particular N is computed in time 2^{(1-eps)n} poly(n,m) whenever r log2(2nB_A+1) + k log2(nB_W+1) + log2(k+1) <= (1-eps) n. PROOF. Key after prefix p: (cnt, y = A x_{<=p}, sorted tuple of (q, s_q) for q in K undecided at p, with exact partial sums s_q = W_{q,<=p}.x_{<=p}). cnt in {0..k} counts exceptional rows already decided TRUE. A row q is decided at p when its future range [minfut, maxfut] lets it be fixed; decided-FALSE rows contribute nothing. Transition: reading x_{p+1} adds A_{.,p+1} to y and W_{q,p+1} to each undecided s_q, then decides rows. Exactness: the future count depends only on the key, because (i) decided exceptional rows are absorbed into cnt; (ii) for an undecided q the future outcome depends only on s_q; (iii) a normal row j satisfies W_j.x = U_j.(A x), so at the end it is decided by U_j.y_n >= t_j with y_n = y_p + A x_{>p}, which depends only on the key and the future bits. Counting: y lies in [-pB_A, pB_A]^r, so (2pB_A+1)^r values; for each q in K the entry is absent or s_q lies in the integer window [t_q - maxfut_q(p), t_q - minfut_q(p) - 1] of size maxfut - minfut <= (n-p)B_W, so at most (n-p)B_W+1 options; cnt gives k+1. Multiplying gives the bound. The DP is exact by (i)-(iii). SCOPE AND LIMITS: (a) needs k log2(nB_W+1) + r log2(2nB_A+1) <= (1-eps)n, so it covers rank r on all but k = o(n/log n) rows, not full-rank W (k=0, r=n fails). (b) Entry-spread error across all columns is NOT covered (G0012, G0013 remain open). (c) Whether hard m = n^alpha THR o THR families have all but o(n/log n) gates in an o(n/log n)-dim row span is open (G0002, G0006). proved_step: PREFIX-RANK STATE LEMMA (general, no factorisation). Let W be an m x n integer matrix with all entries in [-L, L], L >= 1. For 1 <= p <= n let rho_p = rank over Q of the prefix block W[:, 1..p]. Then the number of distinct prefix states {W[:,1..p] x : x in {0,1}^p} is at most min(2^p, (2Lp+1)^{rho_p}). PROOF: choose rho_p linearly independent rows R (a rho_p x p integer matrix) of the prefix block. Every other row of the prefix block is a rational combination of R, row_j = sum_i lambda_{ji} R_i, with lambda fixed by W and independent of x. So W_j,<=p x = sum_i lambda_{ji} (R_i x), and the whole state is a function of R x in Z^{rho_p}. Each entry of R x lies in [-Lp, Lp], a set of 2Lp+1 integers, so at most (2Lp+1)^{rho_p} values. The bound 2^p is trivial. Consequence: if rho_p * log2(2Ln+1) <= (1-eps) n for every prefix that is used, the state count is at most 2^{(1-eps) n}. SCOPE: this is S0081 with the hypothesis A,U,E replaced by 'the prefix rank is small'; for W of total rank r it gives rho_p <= r. It does NOT help full-rank W (rho_p = p gives only the trivial bound), and it does not handle near-low-rank W = UA+E unless the rank of W itself is small.

lemma: Linear prefix-state limit. Let A be an integer m x p matrix with entries in [-B, B], rank r over Q, and let N(A) = number of distinct vectors Ax over x in {0,1}^p. Claim (a): N(A) = 2^p iff ker_Q(A) contains no nonzero vector of {-1,0,1}^p; in particular rank p implies N(A) = 2^p. Claim (b): 2^r <= N(A) <= min(2^p, (2Bp+1)^r) for every such A.

proved_step: LEMMA D1 (exact linear prefix-state limit). Claim (a): A x = A y iff A t = 0 with t = x - y in {-1,0,1}^p. Every nonzero t in {-1,0,1}^p arises as x - y with x = max(t,0) and y = max(-t,0), both in {0,1}^p, and x != y. So x -> Ax is injective on {0,1}^p iff no nonzero such t lies in ker A. If rank A = p then ker A = 0, so N(A) = 2^p. Claim (b), lower bound: pick r columns S with A_S of rank r. A_S is injective on Q^r, so the 2^r vectors A x with x in {0,1}^S (zero outside S) are distinct. Claim (b), upper bound: pick r linearly independent rows R of A. Every row of A is a rational combination of R, so A = M R with M rational, hence Ax = M(Rx). Each entry of Rx lies in [-Bp, Bp], so N(A) <= #{Rx} <= (2Bp+1)^r. The 2^p bound is trivial. Consequence: any DP whose state is the linear prefix vector Ax has at least 2^{rank A} states, and full-rank prefix blocks give exactly 2^p states. The rank DP saves only when r log2(2Bp+1) < p. This identifies the exact limit of the linear-state method and corrects the earlier open reading of G0003: for linear states the full-rank case is settled negatively, so any saving must come from non-linear state (thresholds or clipping) or from a different decomposition.

proved_step: LEMMA (rank-r Cramer DP, exact, no factor hypothesis). Let n, m, r >= 1, W in Z^{m x n} with rank W = r and B = max |W_ji|, B >= 1. Let t, v in Z^m and T in Z. Then N(W,t,v,T) = #{x in {0,1}^n : sum_j v_j [W_j . x >= t_j] >= T} is computable exactly in time poly(m, n, log B) * (2an+1)^r, where a = r^{(r+1)/2} B^r. PROOF. (1) Choose rows R and columns C with Q = W[R,C] nonsingular (|R| = |C| = r; exists since rank r). Put d = det Q != 0 and N := adj(Q) W[R,:] in Z^{r x n}. (2) For every row j: W[j,C] = alpha_j^T Q for alpha_j = Q^{-T} W[j,C]^T, and W[R,:] has rank r, so W_j = W[j,C] Q^{-1} W[R,:]. Multiplying by d: d W_j = c_j N with c_j := W[j,C] in Z^{1 x r}. (3) Hence for y := N x in Z^r: W_j . x >= t_j iff c_j . y >= d t_j when d > 0 (reversed when d < 0). The right side is an integer, so this test is exact. Define g_j(y) := [sign(d)(c_j . y - d t_j) >= 0]. (4) The count equals sum over y of c_n(y) * [sum_j v_j g_j(y) >= T], where c_p(y) = #{x_{<=p} : N_{<=p} x_{<=p} = y}. Each c_p is computed by the recurrence c_{p+1}(y) = c_p(y) + c_p(y - N_{:,p+1}), with states y in Z^r. (5) Bounds: |N_ki| <= r * max|minor_{r-1}(Q)| * B <= r * (r-1)^{(r-1)/2} B^{r-1} * B <= a. Hence |y_k| <= a p at prefix p, and the number of states is at most (2ap+1)^r (and at most 2^p). Total work: O(n S r + S m r) integer operations with S = (2an+1)^r, plus polynomial Gaussian elimination over Q to find R, C, Q. Correctness is exact, since every step is an identity over Z. CONSEQUENCES: (a) for constant r and B = poly(n) the time is poly(n); (b) the time is 2^{(1-eps) n} poly whenever r * log2(2an+1) <= (1-eps) n, i.e. r (log2(2n+1) + ((r+1)/2) log2 r + r log2 B + 1) <= (1-eps) n. For B = O(1) this holds for r <= c sqrt(n / log n). The lemma replaces the hypothesis 'W = UA with small A' of the CLAIMED rank-r DP, and it does not need the factor bound to be an input.

proved_step: L-PROD: CLAIMED. Proof. (1) Rows of R form a Q-basis of the row space, so each row k satisfies A_k = sum_{i in R} c_{k,i} A_i with rational c_{k,i}. Hence (Ax)_k = sum_i c_{k,i} (A_R x)_i, so Ax is a function of A_R x. (2) Thus N(A) <= |{A_R x : x in {0,1}^p}|. (3) For each i in R, (A_i x) is an integer in [sum_j min(a_ij,0), sum_j max(a_ij,0)], an interval of length ||A_i||_1, so it takes at most 1 + ||A_i||_1 values. (4) The image A_R x lies in the product of these intervals, which gives the product bound. (5) ||A_i||_1 <= Bp gives (1+Bp)^r; 2^{(1-eps)p} follows from r log2(1+Bp) <= (1-eps) p. proved_step: THEOREM (rank-r DP). Let W in Z^{m x n} with |W_jl| <= B, rank_Q(W) = r, and let t_j, v_j, T be rationals/integers. Then N = #{x in {0,1}^n : sum_j v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T} is computed exactly in O(n * m * r * (2Bn+1)^r) rational operations on numbers of bit-size poly(n, log B). PROOF. (1) Greedily choose row indices I = {k_1..k_r} with W_{k_1..k_r} linearly independent; they span the row space of W. (2) For each j there is a unique c_j in Q^r with W_j = sum_l c_jl W_{k_l} (existence: spanning; uniqueness: independence). (3) Put s(x) = W_I x in Z^r. Then W_j.x = c_j.s(x), so [W_j.x >= t_j] = [c_j.s(x) >= t_j] depends only on s(x). Hence N = sum_s D(s) g(s), where D(s) = #{x : W_I x = s} and g(s) = [sum_j v_j [c_j.s >= t_j] >= T]. (4) DP over columns i = 1..n: D_0 = delta_0, D_i(s) = D_{i-1}(s) + D_{i-1}(s - col_i), where col_i = (W_{k_l,i})_l. This is exact. (5) For x in {0,1}^n, |W_{k_l}.x| <= Bn, so every reachable state lies in [-Bn, Bn]^r: at most (2Bn+1)^r states at each step. (6) For r <= (1-eps) n / log2(2Bn+1), (2Bn+1)^r <= 2^{(1-eps)n}. With B = poly(n) this range is r = (1-eps) n / O(log n), for any m (m enters only polynomially). The coefficient denominators have bit-size O(r log(Bn)) = poly(n), so the arithmetic overhead is polynomial. SCOPE: exact rank r only. Full rank (G0001 iii) and near-low-rank (G0001 i) are NOT covered. The bound uses only r, not the structure of the thresholds. SUPERSEDES: the sqrt(n/log n) range in the earlier gap, which came from a Hadamard bound on coefficients that the argument does not need. EVIDENCE: exact correctness only, cm-f7bdefcc1a624fd1 (120 random rank<=3 instances, n in 3..8, DP vs brute force, 0 failures). Timing is exploration only and is not cited as support for speed. Correctness is also proved by (1)-(4). thr2_evaluate measurement is pending; its families are generic full-rank, so it cannot test this subclass as provided.

lemma: Cover-rank lemma. Let W in Z^{m x n} with W = P + E, rank(P) <= r, and suppose every nonzero entry of E lies in a row indexed by R or a column indexed by C. Then rank(W) <= r + |R| + |C|. Consequence: exact #SAT of THR o THR with bottom matrix W is computed in time poly(m,n) (2Bn+1)^{rank W}, where B bounds |entries| of W, by the rank-r DP lemma applied with r := rank W. Saving 2^{(1-eps) n} iff r + |R| + |C| <= (1-eps) n / log2(2Bn+1).

proved_step: CLAIMED. Proof of the rank bound: let E_R be E restricted to rows in R and E_C = E - E_R. The nonzero entries of E_C lie in columns of C, so rank(E_C) <= |C|. E_R has at most |R| nonzero rows, so rank(E_R) <= |R|. By subadditivity, rank(W) <= rank(P) + rank(E_R) + rank(E_C) <= r + |R| + |C|. The #SAT consequence uses the rank-r DP with a basis of rank(W) independent rows: the vector of clipped partial sums of the basis rows determines every other row's partial sum, because each row is a rational combination of the basis rows, so the DP is determinate and has at most (2Bn+1)^{rank W} states.

Then N = #{x in {0,1}^n : sum_j v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T} is computed exactly with at most 2^s (2Bn+1)^r reachable states per column step, i.e. O(n m r 2^s (2Bn+1)^r) rational operations. PROOF. Enumerate the prefix xs in {0,1}^s (2^s choices). For fixed xs, the prefix contribution g_j(xs) = sum_{i<=s} W_ji xs_i is a fixed integer. Apply steps (1)-(5) of S0106 to W' (rows I of W' span its row space; W'_j = sum_l c_jl W'_{k_l}; state sv = W'_I x_suffix in Z^r with |sv_l| <= B(n-s)). Then W_j.x = c_j.sv + g_j(xs), so the indicator depends only on (xs, sv). Summing the DP counts over states with the condition gives N exactly. The state count is at most 2^s (2Bn+1)^r. lemma: L1 (weight-free sign-pattern count, rank r). Let W in Q^{m x n} have rank r >= 1, t in Q^m, sigma(x) = (1[W_j . x >= t_j])_{j<=m}. Then |{sigma(x) : x in {0,1}^n}| <= min(2^n, sum_{i=0}^{r} C(m,i)). Proof: factor W = UA (U in Q^{m x r}, A in Q^{r x n}); Y = {Ax : x in {0,1}^n} is finite; delta = min |U_j . y - t_j| over y in Y with U_j . y != t_j (delta = 1 if none); s_j = t_j - delta/2. For y in Y, U_j . y >= t_j implies U_j . y > s_j, and U_j . y < t_j implies U_j . y <= t_j - delta < s_j, so sigma(x)_j = 1[U_j . y(x) > s_j] and no Y-point lies on any hyperplane {U_j . y = s_j}. Hence sigma(x) is the sign vector of a cell of the arrangement of m affine hyperplanes in R^r; distinct cells have distinct sign vectors; the arrangement has at most sum_{i<=r} C(m,i) cells (Buck 1943 / Zaslavsky). Zero rows U_j = 0 give constant signs and do not increase the count.
gap: Does NOT close G0001(iii), G0003 or G0075. A saving for #SAT needs, in addition, a procedure that counts x in {0,1}^n per cell with cost below 2^{(1-eps)n}. proved_step: L2 (meet-in-the-middle with partition-tree range counting, constant rank r). Let W = UA with U in Z^{m x r}, A in Z^{r x n}, t in Z^m, v in Z^m, T in Z; f(x) = [sum_j v_j [U_j.(Ax) >= t_j] >= T]. Fix r >= 1 constant. Split x = (x1, x2) with x1 in {0,1}^h, x2 in {0,1}^u, h + u = n, and let Y2 = {A_2 x2 : x2 in {0,1}^u} (a weighted point set of at most 2^u points in R^r). Then #f = sum over x1 of W(Y2 + A_1 x1), where W(z) = number of points of Y2 with [U_j.(z+y) >= t_j] pattern giving F=1. Claim: the cells of the arrangement {U_j.z = t_j - U_j.(A_1x1)} partition R^r into O(m^r) cells, each triangulated into O(m^r) simplices in total (constant r), and the weighted count of Y2 in each simplex is one simplex-range-counting query (Matousek 1992 partition tree: O(N) preprocessing, O(N^{1-1/r} polylog) per query, constant r). Hence the total time is 2^u * poly(n) (preprocessing) + 2^h * m^{O(r)} * 2^{u(1-1/r)} * poly(n, L) (queries, L = bit length, arithmetic only). Balancing u = h... exactly: the two exponents are u and n - u/r; choosing u = rn/(r+1) gives time 2^{rn/(r+1)} * poly(n, L) * m^{O(r)}. For r = 1 this is 2^{n/2} (consistent with the rank-one result, Q-9d5ab93ad8 / LIT-10). For constant r it is 2^{(1-eps) n} with eps = 1/(r+1), independent of the weight magnitudes. Corollary: for r = n^{1/3} (if the constants of the partition tree are controlled) the saving is 2^{n^{2/3}}, i.e. 2^n / n^{omega(1)}; NOT claimed here (the constants grow with r).

Statement: for any d >= 0, m >= 0 and real affine functions f_1..f_m on R^d (f_j(x) = a_j.x - t_j, a_j = 0 allowed), the set P = { (1[f_j(x) >= 0])_{j<=m} : x in R^d } has |P| <= S(m,d) := sum_{i=0}^{d} C(m,i). PROOF by induction on m, all d at once. Base m=0: |P| = 1 = S(0,d). Base d=0: R^0 is one point, |P| <= 1 = S(m,0). Step m>=1, d>=1: let P' = patterns of f_1..f_{m-1} (the projection of P) and D = {p' in P' : both (p',0) and (p',1) lie in P}. Then |P| = |P'| + |D|. Case a_m = 0: f_m has constant sign, so D is empty and |P| = |P'| <= S(m-1,d) <= S(m,d). Case a_m != 0: H = {x : f_m(x) = 0} is an affine hyperplane isomorphic to R^{d-1}. Let p' in D be realised by x with f_m(x) >= 0 and y with f_m(y) < 0. Put z = (1-s)x + s y with s = f_m(x)/(f_m(x)-f_m(y)) in [0,1); then f_m(z) = 0, so z in H. Each f_j (j<m) is affine, so f_j(z) = (1-s) f_j(x) + s f_j(y). If p'_j = 1, both terms are >= 0, so f_j(z) >= 0; if p'_j = 0, both are < 0, so f_j(z) < 0. Hence z in H realises p' under the closed convention, so D lies in the pattern set of the m-1 restricted functions on H = R^{d-1}, and by induction |D| <= S(m-1,d-1). Therefore |P| <= S(m-1,d) + S(m-1,d-1) = S(m,d) by Pascal's rule C(m-1,i)+C(m-1,i-1) = C(m,i). QED. proved_step: LEMMA L3 (sign-pattern bound, weight-free, rank r). Let W in Z^{m x n} have rank r over Q, t in Z^m, and for x in {0,1}^n put sigma(x)_j = [W_j . x >= t_j] in {0,1}^m. Then |{sigma(x) : x in {0,1}^n}| <= sum_{i=0}^{r} C(m,i). PROOF. Choose r linearly independent rows B of W; every row satisfies W_j = C_j B with C_j in Q^r. Put s = Bx in Z^r. Then W_j . x - t_j = C_j . s - t_j. Let D >= 1 be a common denominator of all C_j, so C_j . s - t_j lies in (1/D) Z for s in Z^r. Set tau_j = t_j - 1/(2D). Then C_j . s - tau_j lies in (1/D)Z + 1/(2D), which never equals 0, so sigma(x)_j = [C_j . s > tau_j] and no lattice point lies on any hyperplane H_j = {s : C_j . s = tau_j}. Hence sigma(x) is the sign vector of the cell of the affine arrangement {H_1..H_m} in R^r containing the point Bx. The number of cells of an arrangement of m affine hyperplanes in R^r is at most sum_{i<=r} C(m,i) (Buck 1943 / Zaslavsky 1975; induction R(m,r) <= R(m-1,r) + R(m-1,r-1), R(0,r) = R(m,0) = 1, which solves to the sum). QED. SCOPE: any integer W of rank r, any integer thresholds, any n; no weight-size assumption. The bound counts distinct SIGN PATTERNS of the full input x. It is not a bound on the number of DP states of a prefix-by-prefix dynamic program, and it does not bound the number of residual functions of a prefix.

proved_step: LEMMA (lane D, variable-class count, CLAIMED by the session that stated it, not yet reviewed). Let C(x) = [sum_j v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T] on {0,1}^n, with integer weights. Suppose the variables partition into D classes C_1..C_D with sizes n_d >= 1, sum n_d = n, and every i in C_d has the same weight column c_d in Z^m (W_{j,i} = c_{d,j}). Then #SAT(C) = sum over 0<=y_d<=n_d of prod_d binom(n_d,y_d) * [sum_j v_j [sum_d y_d c_{d,j} >= t_j] >= T]. Proof: the map x -> (y_d = |x intersect C_d|) is onto, the fibre over y has prod_d binom(n_d,y_d) elements, and W_j.x = sum_d c_{d,j} y_d depends only on y. The sum has prod_d (n_d+1) terms, each costing O(mD). Bound: for x >= 1, x - log2(x+1) >= 0.415 (x-1). This holds with equality at x=2, and the derivative of the left side, 0.585, exceeds that of the right side, 1/((x+1) ln 2), for x >= 2. Multiplying over d gives prod_d (n_d+1) <= 2^{n - 0.415 (n-D)}. Therefore #SAT(C) is computable in time poly(m,D) * 2^{0.585 n + 0.415 D}, a saving of 2^{0.415 (n-D)} over brute force. The saving is superpolynomial iff n - D = omega(log n). For D = O(1) the algorithm is polynomial. Measured counts agree with the bound at all six grid points (cm-b15e97e20ccf4808, cm-7e78b5662f2d4e56).

lemma: RANK-r SUBCLASS (exact, scope: m x n integer matrix W with |W_jk| <= B, rank r over Q). Choose r linearly independent rows R of W, with pivot columns P such that R[:,P] is invertible. Every row satisfies W_j = lambda_j R with lambda_j = W_j[P] (R[:,P])^{-1} in Q^r, because W_j lies in the row space of R. For x in {0,1}^n put y = Rx in Z^r; then |y_k| <= B n and W_j.x = lambda_j . y. Hence #SAT = sum over y in Z^r of N(y) * [ sum_j v_j [lambda_j . y >= t_j] >= T ], where N(y) = #{x : Rx = y}. N is computed by the 0/1 DP over the n columns of R, with states y in Z^r, at most (2Bn+1)^r states, and time O(n r (2Bn+1)^r) plus O(m r (2Bn+1)^r) exact rational evaluations. Corollary: for B = O(1) and r <= eps n / log2 n, the time is 2^{(eps+o(1)) n} poly(n,m), which is a saving of 2^{(1-eps-o(1))n} = n^{omega(1)} over brute force. Proof of the corollary: r log2(2Bn+1) = (eps n / log2 n)(log2 n + O(1)) = eps n (1+o(1)).
